title: Let the purchases in flight finish before the sign-off

blocks.text: Every release of the acquirer's client stops Q2, and every release leaves the same trail:

items: two or three purchases that the host approved come back `null` to the payment service, which reverses them while their cardholders are told they failed;
the host's operators find purchases that arrived on link `acq-mux` after it had been signed off;
on the night of a release when the host had hung, the stop never finished, and the release was rolled back by hand.

blocks.text: `LinkStop.stop()` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkStop.java` is what the sign-on manager runs for each link when Q2 stops it. `disable`, `signOff` and `forget` already work. Finish `stop` and `drain`, the two methods marked `TODO`. `stop` returns how many requests were still waiting for an answer when the sign-off went out, for the operator's log. About ten lines in total.
The tests run a real QMUX against a host on the far side of its queues, which can hold a purchase without answering it. The `Pause` they give you takes no time.

cases.says: a signed-on link with nothing in flight is signed off, its marks are removed and the ready entry stays
a connection that never signed on gets no 0800 / 002, and its marks are removed
the sign-off goes out only after the purchase in flight has its answer, so the purchase completes
the link is out of the pool before the drain starts, so nothing new reaches it while it drains
a request that never gets an answer stops the drain only for the allowed number of pauses; the link is signed off anyway and the request is reported
with nothing in flight the stop does not pause at all
the drain ends as soon as nothing is pending, rather than waiting a fixed time

origin.section: 15.4 Drain a Link Before You Sign It Off

concepts: A planned stop disables the link, waits with a bound until no request is pending, then signs off and forgets the session; without the drain, approvals in flight are lost and reversed.
